solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Describing features of group, very friendly at first

blocks.note: friends who are close are said to be thick, as in 'thick as thieves'
a set is a group of people or things

explanation.surface: A description of some band, whose members were extremely chummy to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' tells you the friendly word goes in front of the group word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset describes a stocky, heavily built body, so it is a word describing someone's physical build.

clue.text: Knowing river creature

blocks.note: hip means in the know, fashionably aware
the Po is the great river of northern Italy, a crossword favourite

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'river creature' as one phrase, which fits nicely, since hippopotamus is Greek for 'river horse'; but 'river' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a large African mammal that lives in rivers, its name meaning river horse.

clue.text: Can tell ref's awfully disappointed

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a messed-up order

blocks.note: the letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A footballer notices the referee looks badly let down by something.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen means dejected, downcast after a setback, like a bird whose crest has drooped.

clue.text: Outline of what may happen currency unit mostly used in South Africa port

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something used in another thing is put inside it

blocks.note: a cent is a hundredth of a dollar or euro
SA is the standard abbreviation for South Africa
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, often shortened

explanation.surface: A forecast of the money that might be spent in a South African harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a sketch or plan of a possible sequence of events.

clue.text: Classic article, excellent, of Hellenic character exactly reproduced

blocks.note: the definite article
sound means solid, of good quality
taken as written
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is used to show a quotation is copied exactly as found

explanation.surface: A fine classic text in Greek, faithfully copied.
explanation.walkthrough: Hellenic means Greek, and a character here is a letter of its alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sound of Music is a much-loved 1965 film musical, a screen classic.

clue.text: One exhibiting sports centre facility?

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who shows something
second meaning: where you wash after exercise

explanation.walkthrough: The word is read two ways: one who shows (rhyming with 'go') and a wash cubicle (rhyming with 'flower').
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, it names someone who displays things and the spray bath found in any gym changing room.

clue.text: Model that one should not miss

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who poses for an artist
second meaning: an easy chance, especially an easy catch in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: In sport a sitter is a chance so easy that missing it is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sits for a portrait is a sitter, and an easy shot or catch is also called a sitter.

clue.text: United about energy

blocks.note: on means concerning, about a subject
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A football club concerned with its stamina levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who are united are said to be one, joined together in agreement.

clue.text: Trainee, not content to leave, upset host

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside, and if that leaves only the outside remains
upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
only the first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A disgruntled apprentice, unhappy about being made to go, upsets the party giver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content to leave' looks like 'happy to go', but it means the middle of the word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To host guests is to entertain them, receiving and looking after them.

clue.text: Special, this place in the round

blocks.note: sp. is a dictionary abbreviation for special
here means at this place

explanation.surface: Something remarkable going on here, in a theatre-in-the-round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a perfectly round solid, a globe or ball, so round works as a noun for it.

clue.text: Ultimately urge new agreement as earnest request

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: the final letter only
N is the abbreviation for new
a treaty is a formal agreement between states

explanation.surface: In the end someone presses for a fresh deal as a heartfelt plea.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal, a request made urgently.

clue.text: Learner revealed as boor

blocks.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate
something revealed is out, in the open

explanation.surface: A student driver is exposed as an uncouth person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is a rough, ill-mannered man, a synonym for boor.

clue.text: Fair and square, refurbished abode? Bravo!

indicators.note: a refurbished place has been done up and rearranged, so the letters are reorganised

blocks.note: the letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: An estate agent cheers an honestly renovated house.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board means honest and open, with nothing concealed, just as fair and square does.

clue.text: Dated former pupil on his own track

blocks.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a British school
sole means belonging to one alone
a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: An old boy of the school out running alone on an old circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolescent describes something becoming out of date, falling out of use, so it is dated.

clue.text: Opportunity for special event

blocks.note: first meaning: a suitable time or chance
second meaning: a celebration or notable function

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a chance to hold a party, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion can be a chance to do something, and also a festive gathering such as a wedding.

clue.text: Climax, enthralling, electric, trios up front seen as potential customers?

indicators.note: a trio is three, and up front means at the start, so three opening letters are taken from each word

blocks.note: the opening three letters
the opening three letters
the opening three letters

explanation.surface: A thrilling, electric finish with three musicians at the front might pull in a paying crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Usually 'up front' takes one initial letter; 'trios' raises it to three letters per word.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of customers a business serves or hopes to attract.

clue.text: Rascal's unending racket

indicators.note: with no ending, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a scamp is a mischievous rogue

explanation.surface: A rogue's never-ending dishonest business.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a fraudulent scheme for making money, just like a scam.

clue.text: Rivalry at event developed over days

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as printed
D is the abbreviation for days

explanation.surface: A competitive grudge built up at a sporting fixture over several days.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long-running bitter feud, an extreme form of rivalry.

clue.text: Determination of wife having complaint

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
an ill is an ailment or complaint

explanation.surface: A spouse's resolve while suffering from some illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Will is resolve or strength of purpose, as in 'where there's a will there's a way'.

clue.text: Admirer, first to last, also describing journey

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved to the final position

blocks.note: a lover is one who admires someone
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A fan, first and last, is also writing an account of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Overland describes travel by land rather than by sea or air, so it is a word describing a journey.

clue.text: Quiet hate seeing winner here?

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quiet
odium is hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: Silently loathing the sight of a rival who won.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the winner stands on the top step.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is the raised platform where medal winners stand at a ceremony.

clue.text: Lacking knowledge, firm undone badly

indicators.note: done badly means done wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A clueless company ruined through poor management.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninformed has not been told the facts, so they are ignorant of them.

clue.text: Troops not half had

indicators.note: not half means only half survives, so the back four letters go

blocks.note: troops are soldiers

explanation.surface: An army unit that was only partly possessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' is the slang sense, as in 'I've been had', meaning cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sold a pup or sold down the river means being tricked, so sold matches had in the sense of conned.

clue.text: Caterpillar, maybe, popular variety to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so the letters lie within part of the words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A caterpillar is perhaps a somewhat well-liked kind of creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is an example of a larva, the young stage of a butterfly or moth.

clue.text: Pottery scarce unfortunately, I'm going back inside

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters fall out of order
going back means read in the opposite direction
inside means placed within the other letters

blocks.note: the letters taken as printed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laments that good pots are hard to find and they are heading home empty-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics are articles made from fired clay, the products of pottery.

clue.text: I see pathway on regular basis

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a footpath they use routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha is an exclamation of sudden understanding, the same as saying I see.

clue.text: Speculative view of politician fellow included

indicators.note: included means taken in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
he refers to a male, a fellow

explanation.surface: A politician's opinion, with a colleague brought in to share it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea or hypothesis put forward to explain something, not yet proved.

clue.text: Make less worried, producing Malbec supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bending flexibly, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: Handing out red wine to settle someone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: Malbec is a red grape and wine; 'supply' is read as 'in a supple way', not as a stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to make calm or still, so it can mean to soothe someone's anxiety.

clue.text: Show appreciation of devious ploy? Nonsense

blocks.note: audiences clap to show they enjoyed something
a trap is a trick to catch someone out

explanation.surface: Applauding a sly scheme, then dismissing it as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, a word for nonsense.
